title: Coral and the Inheritance
premise: Ada Hartwell, a night-shift dispatcher for Coral City Taxi, receives a prepaid booking from a nervous client named Elias Voss who asks her to prove that his sister will not be murdered in three days' time — because the killer's plan is already written into the company's own dispatch ledger. As Ada decodes the coded fare entries, she discovers the conspiracy reaches her beloved mentor, dispatch chief Ruth Calloway, whose loyalty to the family that saved her decades ago forces Ada to choose between exposing the truth and protecting the only person who ever believed in her. In the end Ada broadcasts the decoded ledger over the taxi radio net, Ruth sacrifices herself to stop the final hit, and Ada inherits both Ruth's post and the burden of the secrets she chose to keep.
about_author: Kestrel Ravensworth spent seven years answering phones at a harbor-town cab company before turning the voices in her headset into fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary workers who stumble into extraordinary crimes, drawn from the graveyard shift's strange intimacy with a city after dark.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On a rain-slicked night shift, dispatcher Ada Hartwell takes an odd prepaid booking: Elias Voss wants a car watched on his sister's street for three nights, paid double, no questions. His terror feels specific, rehearsed. The beat is unease — Ada has heard every excuse riders make, but never someone buying protection against a murder that hasn't happened yet.

chapters.title: Three Nights, One Address
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada assigns driver Marisol to stake out the Voss house on Halden Street. Nothing happens the first night except a black sedan that logs itself as a fare that was never called. Ada checks the dispatch ledger and finds the phantom entry already recorded — dated tomorrow. Emotional beat: the first cold drop of dread.

chapters.title: Entries That Haven't Happened
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Digging back through six months of ledgers, Ada finds dozens of fares logged before they occurred, all clustered around deaths later ruled accidental. Someone inside Coral City Taxi has been scheduling murders as routine rides. Beat: vertigo — the familiar job turns predatory.

chapters.title: Elias Explains Too Little
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Ada and Elias. Ada confronts Elias at a diner; he admits his sister Lena is set to testify against the Ashcombe family, who quietly own half the taxi company through a holding firm. He won't say how he knows the date. Beat: reluctant alliance, trust extended but not earned.

chapters.title: Ruth's Steady Hand
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Dispatch chief Ruth Calloway — who pulled teenage Ada off the streets and gave her this job — notices Ada pulling old ledgers and gently warns her not to dig into accounts above her pay grade. Warmth laced with threat. Beat: Ada's loyalty begins to war with her suspicion.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Fares
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Working Marisol's night routes, Ada cracks the system: zone numbers, passenger counts, and tip amounts form a code marking targets, dates, and assigned drivers. The next entry is Lena Voss, three days out, driver code 'K-9'. Beat: grim triumph curdling into helplessness.

chapters.title: Driver Nine
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol realizes her cab number matches K-9 and that she's been assigned a 'special charter' she never accepted. Terrified of the Ashcombes, who bankrolled her brother's medical debts, she almost flees town. Beat: the price of survival made flesh in someone Ada loves.

chapters.title: A Fare Called Ruth
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada traces the oldest coded entries and finds Ruth's handwriting initiating them twenty years ago — starting the week after the Ashcombes paid off Ruth's husband's killers' debts. Beat: heartbreak; the mentor becomes the prime suspect.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ruth's POV, 2001. Young Ruth, drowning in debt after her husband's death, makes her first terrible arrangement with Victor Ashcombe: one 'logistical favor' in exchange for her family's survival. Beat: tragic inevitability — how a good person is conscripted.

chapters.title: Lena Won't Run
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Lena. Ada begs Lena to skip testimony and leave town; Lena refuses — running means the Ashcombes win and Elias stays under their thumb forever. Beat: love against duty crystallized between the sisters and mirrored in Ada's choice about Ruth.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Halden Street
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Night two of the watch: the black sedan returns, and Ada tails it to the Ashcombe marina office, photographing Victor meeting the man who'll play K-9's backup. She's seen leaving. Beat: rising tension, the hunter glimpses her.

chapters.title: Marisol's Confession
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Cornered by an Ashcombe lieutenant reminding her of her brother's debts, Marisol tells Ada everything: the 'charter', the route, the signal phrase she's supposed to radio when Lena is aboard. Beat: fear weaponized; loyalty tested from below.

chapters.title: The Signal Phrase
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada hatches a plan: intercept the hit by faking the radio signal and rerouting the car. But executing it requires access to the master dispatch console — which sits beside Ruth's desk. Beat: scheming under the gaze of the woman she must deceive.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet Rides
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Ruth. Ruth, aware Ada knows, finally tells her partial truth: she's been logging the hits to keep them 'clean', minimizing collateral deaths, trading small evils to keep the machine from worse. Beat: moral fog — the villain argument that almost works.

chapters.title: Elias Is Taken
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elias disappears hours before Lena's testimony; a coded entry appears in the ledger with his description and no destination. The Ashcombes are cleaning loose ends early. Beat: panic, clock accelerating, guilt for bringing him in.

chapters.title: Night Shift Coup
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada seizes the console during shift change, fakes the K-9 signal, and reroutes the hit car to a police checkpoint instead of the courthouse route. It half-works: the driver is caught, but Victor's backup man escapes with Elias. Beat: adrenaline high undercut by cost.

chapters.title: Victor's Offer
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Victor. Summoned to the marina, Ada is offered Ruth's job and silence: the Ashcombes survived every scandal because people like her choose survival over truth. She thinks of Ruth, of Marisol's brother, of Elias missing. Beat: temptation rendered sincerely.

chapters.title: Where They Keep Him
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol decodes a fresh entry — a 'storage charter' to the Ashcombe boatyard — and realizes Elias is held there. Choosing Ada over her debts, she radios the location openly, burning herself with the family. Beat: redemption through sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Boatyard
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax begins: Ada and Ruth, unexpectedly side by side, raid the boatyard. Victor's men corner them; Ruth reveals she's been feeding evidence to a state investigator for a year, using her log-keeping as insurance. Beat: reversal — the traitor was building a case all along.

chapters.title: Calloway's Last Dispatch
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. To cover Ada and Elias's escape, Ruth broadcasts the entire decoded ledger over the open taxi frequency — confessing her twenty years on air — then blocks the Ashcombe men's escape route with her cab. She doesn't survive the crash. Beat: devastating climax; duty fulfilled at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With the broadcast as evidence, Victor Ashcombe falls; Lena testifies safely; Marisol's debts die with the family's leverage. Ada gives the state investigator Ruth's full records, choosing truth even where it stains the woman she loved. Beat: grief braided with vindication.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair Beside Mine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ada runs the night desk from Ruth's chair, training a new hire the way Ruth trained her. A nervous caller asks for a prepaid fare against something that hasn't happened yet. Ada picks up the pencil. Beat: bittersweet resolution — the inheritance continues, eyes open.
